comparison.quote: The best method depends on hair colour, skin tone, treatment area and your goals. Electrolysis is especially useful for light hairs and precise follicle-by-follicle treatment.

hero.title: What is electrolysis?
hero.description: Electrolysis is a hair removal method in which a fine metal probe (needle) is inserted into the hair follicle and an electrical current is passed through it. The current destroys the hair bulb, preventing further hair growth.
methodPoints:
Based on clinical research, official science has recognised electrolysis as the only method of removing hair FOREVER today!!!
The term "permanent hair removal" is exclusive to electrolysis, while photoepilation and laser hair removal are described as "permanent hair reduction".
Electrolysis does not put hair to sleep for a time; it removes it permanently.
Electrolysis can be performed on every skin phototype without exception!
Electrolysis treats every type of hair: vellus, coarse, hormonal, terminal and wiry, regardless of colour: red, blonde, grey or colourless, or texture: curly, wavy, straight or Afro-textured.
Electrolysis can be performed over tattoos (unlike laser).
Electrolysis is safe in the skilled hands of a professional electrologist.
Electrolysis can be used on absolutely any part of the body, without restrictions.
At first, electrolysis may seem expensive, but over several years it can be even more economical than waxing and sugaring.
After a course of electrolysis you will have perfectly smooth skin, without inflammation or ingrown hairs, reduced sweating and confidence in every situation!!

hairGrowthPhases.title: Understanding Hair Growth Cycles
hairGrowthPhases.description: Hair doesn't grow continuously. Understanding these three phases explains why permanent removal requires multiple sessions.
hairGrowthPhases.treatableNote: Only treatment during Anagen results in permanent hair removal.

phases.name: Anagen
phases.subtitle: Growth Phase
phases.description: Hair actively grows from the follicle. This is the only phase when electrolysis can permanently destroy the follicle.

phases.name: Catagen
phases.subtitle: Transition Phase
phases.description: Hair transitions from growth to rest. The follicle begins to separate from the root.

phases.name: Telogen
phases.subtitle: Resting Phase
phases.description: Hair rests in the follicle before shedding. The follicle is dormant and cannot be treated effectively.

multiple.title: Why Multiple Sessions Are Needed
multiple.paragraph1: At any given time, only about 85% of hair is in the Anagen growth phase. The remaining 10-15% is resting and cannot be treated. This means your first appointment treats the actively growing hairs.
multiple.paragraph2: Over the next several weeks, new hairs from other phases will enter Anagen and become visible. These are treated in follow-up sessions until all hairs have been permanently removed. This typically takes 6-12 months.

faq.description: Answers to common questions about electrolysis and your visit.

items.question: What results can I expect from electrolysis?
items.answer: Electrolysis treats individual hair follicles. A course of treatments is usually needed; its length depends on the area and individual factors.

items.question: How long does a session take?
items.answer: Time varies based on the area. Small areas like the upper lip may take 15-30 minutes, while larger areas can take 1-2 hours. I will provide a timeline at our consultation.

items.question: How many sessions will I need?
items.answer: The number of sessions varies by area, hair density, growth cycle, hormones and previous hair-removal methods. Your treatment plan can be refined as progress becomes visible.

items.question: Does it hurt?
items.answer: Sensation varies from person to person and by treatment area. It is often described as brief warmth, tingling or stinging, and comfort can be discussed during your consultation.

items.question: Will there be redness after treatment?
items.answer: Most clients experience minimal redness that fades within hours. I apply soothing products immediately after treatment.

items.question: Does it work on all hair colors?
items.answer: Yes. Electrolysis works on all skin types and all hair colors, including blonde, red, gray, and white. It is the most inclusive method available.

treatmentAdvice.title: Preparation and aftercare
treatmentAdvice.description: A few simple steps can help you prepare and care for your skin. We will discuss advice tailored to you at your consultation.

groups.title: Preparing for your appointment
items: Grow hair to approximately 3–5 mm so it can be grasped with tweezers.
Arrive with clean skin, without cosmetics or deodorant on the treatment area.
Discuss your previous hair removal methods and when to stop using them with your specialist in advance.
Avoid tanning and sunbeds before your visit; let your specialist know if your skin is irritated or broken.

groups.title: After your treatment
items: Keep the skin clean, avoid touching the area with unwashed hands and do not pick any scabs.
Avoid overheating, friction, swimming pools and intense exercise while the skin recovers; ask your specialist about timing.
Protect treated skin from the sun with SPF 30–50; protect your face year-round.
Avoid cosmetics and deodorant on irritated skin; discuss suitable products and when to use them with your specialist.

groups.title: When to ask for advice
items: Before booking, tell your specialist about pregnancy, a pacemaker or other implanted device, medical conditions, medicines, metal allergies, broken skin and a tendency to scar.
Depending on your circumstances, advice from your doctor may be needed; suitability is assessed individually.
Seek medical advice if pain or swelling increases, or if you develop pus or a fever after treatment.
